summary: Requesting audit and manual credit: batch embedding run triggered unbilled cache-hit credits and subsequent reversal
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Verano Health reports an unexpected credit reversal and apparent missing credit application after a large nightly batch embedding job that benefited from prefix/KV cache hits. The customer's March invoice shows a reversal line for 'cache-optimization credit' and an overcharge relative to their expected metering.

Impact:
- Customer reports a ~$18,400 delta between their internal usage estimate and the invoice. They believe many tokens were served from KV/prefix cache and should have incurred reduced billed tokens or been eligible for an optimization credit.
- This is a dedicated-customer (reserved capacity) account on prod-us-east with monthly billing. Customer is concerned about repeated unexpected reversals after infra optimizations.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dh-prod-09 (us-east)
- Model: open-embedding-3-small (quantized)
- Job type: nightly batch embedding (100k documents) using SDK v1.8.3

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Kick off batch run at 00:15 UTC that reads documents and calls /embeddings in parallel with batching.
2) Job observes high KV cache hit rate in runtime metrics (~72% prefix hits) and latency per request drops.
3) Billing dashboard later showed initial metered tokens count, then a system-generated credit reversal (line item: cache-optimization-credit reversal) and final invoice higher than expected.

Observed behavior:
- Initial usage snapshot (03-09 01:00 UTC) showed billed tokens X. By invoice generation (03-10), a reversal line appears and final billed tokens are higher than the initial snapshot would imply. Customer expects lower net cost given high cache hit rates.

Expected behavior:
- Cache hit reductions should reduce effective billed token units or be accounted as optimization credits per the dedicated plan. Any automated reversal should be accompanied by a clear audit entry.

Attachments (provided by customer):
- billing-export-2026-03-09.csv (summary from customer analytics)
- sdk-call-trace.log (trimmed)

Customer request:
- Full audit of metering decisions for the job window 2026-03-09 00:00 to 2026-03-09 04:00 UTC
- Explanation for reversal line and a manual credit if system misapplied billing logic
comments: 2026-03-10 09:24 - Aisha Patel (Support): Ticket created after customer emailed billing@redwood.ai. Added initial artifacts and requested priority review from billing and metering teams.

2026-03-10 10:12 - Diego Morales (Billing): Acknowledged. Assigned to billing metering engineer. Will request the KV/cache hit logs and run cost reconciliation. (ref: slack #support-billing thread t/abc123)

2026-03-10 14:05 - SRE (Jin Park): Noted that dh-prod-09 had a cache rebalancing job at 00:22 UTC that briefly updated prefix cache TTLs. Linking internal run: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Cache+Rebalance+2026-03-09

2026-03-11 08:30 - Diego Morales (Billing): Partial reconciliation: system counted 'cache-optimization-credit' for job window then an automated guard-clause reversed the credit when a downstream consistency check flagged mismatched token signatures. We're pulling the signature mismatch logs for the customer's job.

2026-03-12 11:18 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer asks for transparency on signature mismatch and whether it could be caused by SDK v1.8.3 parallel batching. Customer requests a timeframe for manual credit decision.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses: 1) Rebalance TTL update caused transient cache index changes; reconciliation job later detected keys with mismatched signatures and rolled back credits. 2) SDK parallelization produced out-of-order requests that temporarily surfaced as lower effective token counts in the runtime but didn't meet the strict criteria for automation credits.

Work done so far:
- Pulled runtime logs (kv-cache metrics) for dh-prod-09 00:00-04:00 UTC; observed 68-74% hit rate.
- Queried metering pipelines: initial aggregator emitted a tentative cache-credit event (event_id ccred-20260309-007) then ledger job reversed it via guard (ledger-rev-9912) citing signature mismatch.
- Cross-checked SDK call IDs from customer's sdk-call-trace.log against runtime request IDs: ~98% match; ~2% requests missing call_id fields (likely from older workers triggering fiber restart).
- Raised INT-4153 with infra to check TTL rebalancing side effects.

Open questions for engineering/billing:
- What exact signature criteria caused the ledger reversal? (hash of token windows vs request metadata?)
- Does our credit safety guard require request-level call_id parity? If so, is SDK v1.8.3 guaranteed to set call_id on all retries/parallel shards?
resolution:
Investigating — billing escalation created and infra asked to supply the signature-mismatch audit. Next steps: (1) infra to provide detailed ledger entries and signature deltas (due 2026-03-12 end-of-day); (2) billing to run a manual reconciliation script for the customer's disputed window and propose a manual credit if ledger reversal is found to be overly conservative; (3) recommend customer upgrade to SDK v1.8.5 which contains call_id fixes to avoid missing call_id on retry.

Interim outcome (as of 2026-03-12): Billing confirmed the reversal was triggered by ledger guard, but manual audit is required to determine whether the reversal was appropriate. Customer notified and promised an update by 2026-03-13. If audit finds misapplication, support will issue a manual credit and update the invoice.
